ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZiEOug", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDI53w", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 111, "title": "Add an evidence-qualified electronic-publishing reading journey from MAIN 10", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `f8e1ebf4e5a09b69cfe7a91a738b3e64445adfd6`, MAIN/index selector `10 電子出版` opens a generic collection showing zero publications. Visitors cannot select a publication, browse its contents or read an installment.

This leaves a material service journey absent. Earlier #33 intentionally supplied navigable empty collections; this Issue advances that scope.

## Expected outcome

Provide MAIN or index → `10` → publication directory → `1` original fictional publication → contents with two short connected Japanese fiction installments → `READ 1` / `READ 2` → `LIST` / `BACK` → actual caller.

The publication is bundled, read-only application content, distinct from forum contributions and file acquisition. Its name, prose, secondary placement, numbering, layout and controls are category D reconstruction. It must not impersonate an authentic PC-VAN Journal issue.

## Context

### Historical evidence and tolerance

Sources were inspected on 2026-10-24:

- [NEC PC-VAN office article, March 1993, printed page 232](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jkg/43/3/43_KJ00002959297/_pdf/-char/ja) describes an online magazine offering original fiction in daily installments under information-file services. Confidence is high for this earlier documented category. Its unchanged availability and organization in late 1996 are unverified.
- [Retrospective MAIN reproduction labeled circa 1996](https://paradisearmy.com/doujin/pasok3pc-van.htm) places electronic publishing at selector 10. Confidence is high in the displayed reproduction; historical authenticity and revision chronology remain provisional. It supplies no secondary publishing menu.
- [Windows 95 client-author description](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/win95/net/se024554.html) separately lists paid PC-VAN Journal unread retrieval. Confidence is high in that stated capability, but release dating and target-year applicability remain unresolved. This does not establish that the Journal and the 1993 fiction service were identical.
- The [Information White Paper 1996 search excerpt](https://www.jipdec.or.jp/archives/publications/J0005030.pdf) mentions a Journal full-service launch, but direct retrieval timed out. A [later ASCII biography excerpt](https://ascii.jp/elem/000/000/310/310653/) offers an editorial-history lead; opening failed. Neither supplies implementation requirements, an authenticated launch date or host controls.

Accept moderate confidence in the experiential reconstruction: editorial contents followed by connected installments. Exact 1996 publication inventory, service relationships, host commands, tariffs, subscriptions and paging remain unresolved. Do not borrow exact controls from other services or introduce later web-magazine features.

### Implementation evidence

- `src/sections.ts` maps selector 10 to the empty `publications` collection; selector 20 shares that generic collection kind.
- `src/navigation.ts` currently sends 10 through the generic section handler. Existing news/EIC readers demonstrate bundled bodies, contextual READ handling and actual-parent navigation.
- `tests/sections.spec.ts` explicitly expects 10 to remain empty and reject reading. Update that expectation specifically; preserve selector 20 and other unaffected destinations.
- `tests/news.spec.ts` and `tests/terminal-helpers.ts` provide existing controller, production-terminal, IME, log and protected-record comparison patterns.
- Live repository-scoped open-Issue and open-PR searches returned no items. Publishing-history searches recovered #5 and #33 without an equivalent pending increment.

PR #110 reports 107 focused, 401 complete-suite and 10 subsequent fixture checks passing with three workers. These are Coordinator-reported results, not checks executed by this research graph. Default/eight-worker reliability remains unresolved.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the complete journey above through the existing controller and terminal. Include one clearly named fictional publication, a contents list with stable numbers/titles, and two short original Japanese installments forming a connected story. Avoid fabricated historical issue dates, real author identities and copied archival prose.
- [ ] `HELP` preserves the current view. `LIST` from a body returns to contents; `BACK` follows body → contents → publication directory → actual MAIN/index caller. Repeated or different READ selections replace the body without accumulating duplicate parents. `MAIN` clears the path; reopening starts at the directory.
- [ ] Invalid, missing, malformed and oversized selections preserve the current view and give useful guidance. WRITE/REPLY, purchase, download and connection attempts cannot start composition, acquire files or invoke another service. Preserve application Settings/About/HANDLE/STOP behavior and terminal input ownership.
- [ ] Keep readings outside IndexedDB, backups and resident-generation context. Browsing must not create boards, posts, mail, read markers, publication subscriptions or scheduling state. Preserve anonymous access and populated, imported and deliberately emptied worlds. No schema migration or new inference/network subsystem is needed.
- [ ] Preserve existing functional, storage, consent, calendar, mail, OLT, composition, IME and terminal regression coverage. Selector 20 and other unaffected MAIN destinations retain their behavior.
- [ ] Update README usage/menu mapping, Settings/About and the existing research document. Record source URLs, access date, historical scope, confidence, failed retrievals and category D choices. Explain the uncertain relationship between the earlier online magazine and PC-VAN Journal. Keep normal reading screens concise; provenance belongs in on-demand documentation.
- [ ] Add focused coverage using existing Playwright/controller facilities: both entry parents, both complete bodies, repeated READ, LIST/BACK/MAIN paths, invalid selections, re-entry and service isolation. Exercise the production terminal with anonymous, populated and restored-empty fixtures; compare protected records before/after with consent disabled and a controlled clock, allowing ordinary session/history changes.
- [ ] Verify literal Japanese and line breaks in rendered output and downloaded terminal logs, including harmless angle-bracket text rendered as text. Cover IME Enter protection, Settings return with unfinished input, and the existing narrow-terminal scrolling behavior. Assert that publishing adds no external requests and its bundled bodies do not enter world backups.
- [ ] Run the focused new/affected specs and `npm test -- --workers=3`; the existing configuration performs TypeScript checking and the production build. Record actual results, failures, skips and worker configuration. Check documentation links/anchors and `git diff --check`, then review the complete diff against this scope. No model download or real inference is necessary.

## Optional validation

Comparison with a subsequently recovered dated publishing manual/session and former-user feedback would improve confidence. Native Japanese IME checks are optional beyond automated regression coverage.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.
